best_for: 3D printer owners who tune their own prints, run Bambu, Prusa, Voron or Creality machines, and want free built-in calibration tests instead of printing test files by hand.
description:
OrcaSlicer is a slicer for FDM 3D printers: it prepares your 3D models for printing. SoftFever leads the project, and hundreds of contributors work on it in the open on GitHub.

Before anything reaches the printer, the preview shows each line type with its print time and filament use. On a multi-material plate you assign a filament to each part, see which nozzle will print it, and check how much of each filament the job takes, prime tower included. You can set speed, layer height and temperature separately for walls, infill and supports. A search box jumps straight to any setting by name, so you don't have to dig through tabs.

points.title: Calibration tests are built in
points.text: Flow rate, pressure advance, temperature towers, retraction, tolerance and max volumetric speed tests come in the app. You print the test, read the result and save it to your filament profile.

points.title: Many printers out of the box
points.text: It ships tuned profiles for hundreds of printers, including Bambu Lab, Prusa, Creality, Voron, VzBot and RatRig. It can also send jobs to and watch printers running Klipper, PrusaLink or OctoPrint.

points.title: Fine control over walls and seams
points.text: You get detailed seam placement including scarf seams, sandwich mode, polyholes, mouse-ear brims and adaptive bed mesh, plus belt printer and IDEX support.

points.title: Free, with no account
points.text: OrcaSlicer is open source under AGPL 3.0. The project says it has no account, no telemetry and no lock-in. It builds on Bambu Studio and PrusaSlicer.

points.title: The Bambu plugin is not open
points.text: Extra features for Bambu Lab printers come from an optional network plugin built on Bambu's non-free libraries. You can skip it if you want a fully open setup.

points.title: Watch out for fake download sites
points.text: The project warns that look-alike sites such as orca-slicer[.]com and orcaslicer[.]net pass off risky downloads. Get it from orcaslicer.com, GitHub releases, Flathub, winget or Homebrew.

points.title: Builds for every desktop
points.text: Windows has x64 and Arm64 installers that install for all users and may need the WebView2 runtime. The Mac build is universal. The Linux Flatpak covers x64 and Arm64 and is verified by Flathub as published by SoftFever.

points.title: Rolling back
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 17 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so older builds there come from GitHub releases.
